FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Textile Speciality Chemicals and Dyestuffs Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Textiles Division Council. 


Solubilized vat dyestuffs are increasingly being used in the industry for dyeing and printing of fabrics. 
The strength of solubilized vat dyes is generally determined by comparison with an agreed standard by 
dyeing test which creates difficulties in reporting records of production, import or export statistics, or 
comparing dyes where due to slight shade difference the assessment of strength by dyeing method 
becomes difficult. To overcome this difficulty, this standard has been prepared to determine the strength 
by gravimetric method which agrees with the dyeing tests. The method prescribed is applicable to 
individual dyes but not to a mixture of dyes. It takes care of dyes which are precipitated due to over 
oxidation. However, it may not be very much suitable for dyes which are partially oxidized and pass 
through the filtering media. 


This standard was first published in 1970. The first revision has been made in the light of experience 
gained since its publication and to incorporate the following major changes: 


a) Title of the standard has been modified; 

b) Grade and purity of chemicals used have been specified; 
c) Sampling clause has been modified; and 

d) References to Indian Standard have been updated. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in 
Annex A. 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, 
observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for 
rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. 


IS 5970 : 2022 


Indian Standard 
TEXTILE DYESTUFFS — METHOD FOR ESTIMATION OF 
STRENGTH (VAT CONTENT) OF SOLUBILIZED VAT 
DYESTUFFS 
( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes a gravimetric method for 
the estimation of strength (vat content) of 
homogeneous solubilized vat dyestuffs. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standard contains provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the edition indicated was valid. All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of 
applying the most recent edition of the standard 
indicated below. 


IS No. Title 
1070 : 1992 


Reagent grade water - 
Specification (third revision) 


3SAMPLING 


3.1 Lot — All the containers of the same dye and 
the same strength delivered to a buyer against a 
dispatch note shall constitute a lot. 


3.2 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer 
and the seller the number of containers to be 
selected at random from a lot shall be in 
accordance with Table 1. 


3.3 From each container draw small quantities of 
the dye by a suitable sampling instrument from at 
least three different parts and mix them 
thoroughly to get a composite sample weighing 
about 20 g. This shall constitute the test sample. 


Table 1 Sample Size 
(Clause 3.2) 


Lot Size Sample Size 
(1) (2) 
2 to 15 2 
16 to 25 3 
26 to 50 4 
51 to 100 5 
101 to 150 6 
151 to 300 7 
301 and above 8 


4 APPARATUS AND REAGENTS 


4.1 Sintered Glass Funnel and Crucible — 
porosity G 4. 


4.2 Distilled Water — see IS 1070. 
4.3 Sodium Nitrite Solution — 10 percent (м/у). 
4.4 Dilute Sulphuric Acid — prepared by 


diluting 10 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid to 
100 ml. 


IS 5970 : 2022 


4.5 Unless otherwise specified analytical reagent 
grade chemicals with 99.0 percent purity shall be 
employed in tests and distilled water (see IS 
1070) shall be used where the use of water as 
reagent is intended. 


5 PROCEDURE 


5.1 Take about 2 g of solubilized vat dyestuff and 
weigh it accurately. Dissolve the dyestuff in 200 
ml of distilled water at 60°C. Filter the solution 
while hot through sintered glass funnel of 
porosity G4 type and wash the funnel with hot 
distilled water until the dissolved dyestuff goes 
into the filtrate. 


5.2 Add 10 ml of sodium nitrite solution and 10 
ml of dilute sulphuric acid to the solution 
obtained as in 5.1. Boil for 5 minutes and filter it 
through a previously weighed sintered glass 
crucible of porosity G4 type. Wash the residue on 
the crucible with distilled water till free from acid 
using an appropriate indicator, such as 
bromocresol purple. Dry the crucible along with 
the residue at 100 + 3°C to constant weight. 
Determine the weight of the residue. 


5.3 Repeat the test with at least two more test 


specimens. 
6 CALCULATIONS 


6.1 Calculate the strength of the solubilized vat 
dyestuff by the following formula: 


P=W> х 100 
W; 
Where 


P = percentage by weight of the vat content of 
solubilized vat dyestuff, 

Wı = weight in g of the solubilized vat dyestuff 
taken for the test (see 5.1), and 

W2 = weight in g of the residue obtained as in 5.2. 


6.2 Similarly, calculate the strength of the other 
test specimens and calculate the average of the 
results. 

7 REPORT 


The report shall include the following: 


a) Strength of dyestuff, and 
b) Number of tests. 


IS 5970 : 2022

Review of Indian Standards 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
